locator.text: Equation (5.36), p. 58, in the statement of Lemma 5.4

evidence: paper: \forall m, N \quad \exists \delta, C > 0 \quad |\mathcal{F}(U)|_m \le C q^{N} \qquad (0 < q < \delta).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The quantifier order matches the paper: m and N are arguments of the theorem (so universally quantified) and δ, C are existential in the conclusion, with 0 < q < δ as the domain. The residual hypothesis (5.33) is hypothesis hres (lines 127-129) together with he and Tendsto rho atTop atTop, which reproduces C_{J,m} q^{ρ_J - K^F_m} Λ_log(q)^{P_{J,m}} + E_{J,m} with E flat and ρ_J → ∞; 𝓕 is a SupportedPolynomial P and |𝓕(U)|_m is ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (P.eval (components …))‖. One convention: Lean bounds exactly order m, the paper's |·|_m of (5.23) the max over orders ≤ m; applying the theorem at each k ≤ m and taking the least δ and greatest C over that finite set recovers the paper's form. Lean also allows N : ℝ rather than N ∈ ℕ, and the bound is stated pointwise on x ∈ U rather than over a region, which is the same thing.
